sources.title: NYC LPC Fraunces Tavern Block Historic District, 1978
sources.pages: PDF 2 boundary map; PDF 10,16,17 architectural descriptions
sources.inspection: Individually inspected district map and read the relevant descriptions. The corner tavern is distinct from 101 Broad and 58 Pearl. Three-story building has high buff-brick base, columned portico, twelve-over-twelve sash, red flat arches, paneled cornice, two dormers on each roof side, tall chimneys and roof platform enclosed by balustrade.
Museum account corroborates surviving buff Dutch and red English brick, the restored roofline and 1907 reopening. No claim of a wholly new replica or exact 1783 exterior is made.
